text:
mira: Heads up — eu-west dedicated pool (rack-12) is showing sporadic token tail latency spikes since ~09:10 UTC. Not full OOMs, but 95/99p up ~2-3x for tenant-heavy slices.
jon: Seen the alerts. Any correlation with NVLink saturation or egress queues?
alex: NVLink counters are noisy but not maxed. I pulled some perf traces, looks like periodic PCIe stalls when a batch job does large KV regeneration.
mira: Example from the last spike (09:22):
```
serving_latencies: {p50: 18ms, p95: 240ms, p99: 510ms}
pcie_dropped_frames: +120
kv_regen_rate: 6/s (burst)
```
sam: Is this isolated to dedicated slices or also hitting shared tenants? Costs for migration will be non-trivial if we carve more slices out.
mira: Mostly dedicated slices on rack-12, shared on adjacent racks unaffected. Hypothesis: single noisy tenant in dedicated slice doing heavy k-v churn -> local PCIe storms affecting colocated slots.
jon: Could be a firmware/driver interaction that surfaces under large sized batched -- we saw similar in apac edge months ago. What's the current mitigation?
alex: Short-term: can throttle KV regen on that tenant via proxy config (rate-limit to 1/s) and mark their slice for soft-quarantine (deprioritize burst lanes). Long-term: consider moving that tenant to fractional dedicated with dedicated NIC shaping.
infra-bot: [metric link] cpu/gpu/pcie/e2e tail-traces attached -> https://internal.metrics/shot/1741117777
sam: Throttling is fine if it doesn't break their batch jobs. Any estimate on added infra cost if we migrate them to full dedicated node?
alex: Quick calc: moving off the current fractional slice -> full reserved GPU adds ~0.7k/mo for capacity delta + one-time rebind ops. But it eliminates contention and reduces tail by ~70% per our sims.
mira: Ops plan: 1) Apply soft-quarantine to tenant X now (Jon/Sam ok?) 2) Throttle KV regen via proxy (Alex) 3) Monitor 30m, if tail persists then schedule migration window to spare node later today.
jon: I'm okay with soft-quarantine and throttle. Can we automate detection so noisy KV regen triggers quarantine without manual triage?
alex: We have a detector stub (kv-burst-detector) but it needs a tuning pass to avoid false positives. I can flip it to conservative mode for eu-west racks after the mitigation.
sam: If detector works, we could reduce manual rotations which cut ops cost. Thx.
mira: I'll run the throttle now and tag infra-ops.
jon: ping @sam once the detector is in conservative mode so we don't accidentally migrate legit workloads.
infra-bot: ticket created: INF-4821 "eu-west rack-12 noisy-kv-regeneration" (priority P2). Owner: alex.
alex: throttle applied at 09:34 UTC. Watching dashboards.
mira: After 12m, p95 dropped from 240ms -> 90ms, p99 from 510ms -> 160ms. Looks promising.
sam: Great. Let's keep detector in conservative for 24h and then iterate. When you have the cost numbers for full migration, drop in INF-4821.
mira: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
